summary: Etna sits in the Scott Valley of Siskiyou County, a genuine cattle-and-timber settlement of roughly 670 people wedged between the Marble Mountains to the west and the Scott Mountains to the east — peaks that routinely top 7,000 feet and feed the Scott River running just outside town. With a median home value around $238,400 against a median household income near $60,300, the price-to-income ratio lands below 4:1, a figure that would be almost unrecognizable in most of coastal California; median rent at $854 a month reinforces that affordability, though a poverty rate above 20% signals the local economy is thin. Employment options within town are extremely limited — government services, small retail, ranching, and timber-adjacent work account for most of it, and anything resembling a professional job market requires a long drive toward Yreka or beyond on two-lane mountain roads. The town itself is compact at 0.8 square miles, with a small historic main street, and daily highs averaging 62°F across the year with cold nights dipping to 38°F — winters bring real snow, summers bring 90°F-plus days and wildfire smoke risk common to interior Northern California. Etna is a place where the geography is spectacular and the economy is not, and that tension defines nearly every decision about living there.
